skill.name: hooks-automation
skill.description: Automates Claude Code hook workflows for task preparation, edit validation, formatting, session memory, Git checks, and multi-agent coordination with Claude Flow.
skill.summary: Automates Claude Code hooks for validation, formatting, memory, Git quality gates, and multi-agent coordination.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command examples, and documentation snippets rather than executable Ruby or shell code in the skill. One production environment file example remains a confirmed risk, and semantic review found unsafe hook command interpolation plus possible sensitive command-output persistence. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Hook commands interpolate untrusted tool parameters into shell command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use argument-array execution or strict escaping and allowlist validation for file paths, task text, search patterns, and Bash command values.

remediation.issue: The documentation shows a production environment file being processed with backup enabled.
remediation.suggestion: Replace production.env examples with non-secret sample paths and require explicit manual approval for any environment file access.

remediation.issue: Post-bash output logging and result storage can retain secrets printed by commands.
remediation.suggestion: Disable command output storage by default or add redaction, retention limits, and clear opt-in controls.

remediation.issue: The destructive command validation example uses rm -rf syntax.
remediation.suggestion: Use a harmless placeholder command or state clearly that destructive examples are for validation only and must not be executed.

content.value_statement: Manual hook setup makes multi-step coding workflows hard to keep consistent. This skill explains how to configure Claude Flow hooks for validation, formatting, memory, Git checks, and agent coordination.
actual_capabilities: Documents pre-task, pre-edit, pre-bash, and pre-search hook workflows.
Documents post-edit, post-bash, post-task, and post-search processing flows.
Shows Claude Flow hook commands for formatting, validation, memory storage, and metrics.
Explains session start, session restore, and session end coordination patterns.
Provides Git hook examples for pre-commit, post-commit, and pre-push checks.
Describes MCP-based memory usage, agent spawning, swarm status, and neural training integration.
limitations: It depends on the Claude Flow CLI and local hook support.
MCP examples require compatible servers and permissions.
Configured hooks can run local commands, so users must review each command first.
The skill is documentation only and does not include executable hook source files.

use_cases.title: Standardize Edit Workflows
use_cases.description: Set up hooks that validate files before edits and format code after edits.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Tasks
use_cases.description: Use task and memory hooks to share context across agents during larger changes.

use_cases.title: Add Git Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Connect hook commands to commit and push checks for tests, metrics, and reports.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basic Hooks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to outline a basic Claude Flow hook setup for my repository. Include pre-edit validation, post-edit formatting, and session-end summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Add Edit Safety Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to design pre-edit and post-edit hooks for JavaScript files. Include syntax validation, formatting, memory keys, and protected file review.

prompt_templates.title: Create Git Quality Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to plan pre-commit and pre-push hooks for tests, Claude Flow metrics, and failure handling. Avoid unsafe shell interpolation.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to design a multi-agent workflow with task hooks, memory namespaces, session restore, Git checks, and post-task reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan a basic hook setup for a new web project.
output_examples.output: A staged setup plan covering initialization, pre-edit validation, post-edit formatting, session-end summaries, and manual review points.

output_examples.input: Add safety checks for protected files.
output_examples.output: A review workflow that blocks sensitive files, requests manual approval, and avoids storing secrets in hook memory.
A coordination plan with task preparation, shared memory keys, edit validation, status notifications, and final metrics review.

best_practices: Review every generated hook command before enabling it in a real project.
Use clear memory namespaces and avoid storing secrets or raw command output.
Start with validation and formatting hooks before adding Git or multi-agent automation.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted tool parameters into shell commands without escaping or validation.
Do not enable automatic hooks for secret files or production configuration files.
Do not treat hook metrics as a substitute for tests, reviews, or security scans.

faq.question: Does this skill install Claude Flow?
faq.answer: No. It documents Claude Flow hook usage and assumes the CLI is installed separately.

faq.question: Can it run local commands?
faq.answer: Yes, configured hooks can run local commands through Claude Flow. Review each command before enabling it.

faq.question: Does it support Git hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for pre-commit, post-commit, and pre-push workflows.

faq.question: Does it require MCP servers?
faq.answer: Basic hook concepts do not require MCP servers. MCP coordination examples require compatible server configuration.

faq.question: Can it protect sensitive files?
faq.answer: It describes protected file checks and manual approval flows. Users must configure those controls correctly.

faq.question: Is it safe to enable every example?
faq.answer: No. Treat examples as templates and adapt them with validation, escaping, and secret handling.
